Import customs value of liquid dielectric transformers having a power handling capacity exceeding 100 MVA (HTS 8504.23.0080) between 2015 and 2024 According to Chapter 85 in the 2026 Harmonized Tariff Schedule, Revision 5 (USITC 2024b), imports of LPTs in 2024 were subject to a baseline 0% Most Favored Nation (MFN) duty rate; the same rate applied to U.S. free trade agreement partners Canada and Mexico under the United States–Mexico–Canada Agreement of 2020. However, non-MFN countries could face a 35% duty. Additional trade remedies significantly affect certain suppliers: imports from China incur a 25% Section 301 tariff on top of the customs value, and transformers with significant steel content from specified countries may also be subject to a 25% Section 232 tariff, though exemptions apply for Canada, Mexico, and some other partners. The leading import countries in 2024, such as South Korea, Canada, Mexico, Austria, Germany, and Brazil, benefit from the 0% MFN rate while China faced the mandatory Section 301 duty, and steel tariff applicability varied by origin and product composition. The USITC upholds antidumping and countervailing duties on LPTs from South Korea, citing likely recurrence of material injury to domestic manufacturers in the United States if the duties were revoked (USITC 2024b). These duties on South Korean imports could effectively constrain one of the most cost-effective and competitive foreign sources of LPTs for the U.S. market. 1.8 Supply Challenges Many hydroelectric plants operate for longer than the 40- to 45-year design lifetime of an LPT, which leads to demand for replacement transformers for older hydroelectric plants. Long lead times, high costs, and complex logistics present challenges for hydropower operators who wish to procure replacement LPTs. 15 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. Lead times: The time between placing an order and receiving an LPT has increased from 5–16 months in 2010 to an average of 30 months in the first half of 2025 (Wood Mackenzie 2025; Office of Electricity Delivery and Energy Reliability 2014).
